u0250.gist: PM Modi inaugurated the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan in New Delhi, closing year-long celebrations of 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission.
facts: Inaugurated on October 23, 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; event ran 23–25 October.
Over 9,000 participants from India and abroad were expected.
PM interacted with a 'Holobot' (holographic image) of Swami Chinmayananda; recalled their 1993 Vadodara meeting.
Swami Chinmayananda (born Balakrishna Menon, 8 May 1916; died 3 August 1993) founded Chinmaya Mission in 1953.
His Gita Gyana Yagnas took Bhagavad Gita, Upanishads and Vedanta teachings to the public.
PM's focus: culture, social unity, self-reliance and youth role in Viksit Bharat by 2047.
u0250.check: Mission founded in 1953, yet 75 years are celebrated in 2026 (1953 + 75 would be 2028).

mcq.q: In October 2026, PM Modi inaugurated the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at which venue?
mcq.why: PM inaugurated the Sammelan on October 23, 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.

u0251.gist: UDAN, the regional air-connectivity scheme launched on 21 October 2016, completed 10 years of bringing flights to unserved and underserved areas.
facts: RCS-UDAN = Regional Connectivity Scheme – Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik; follows National Civil Aviation Policy, 2016.
First UDAN flight: Shimla–Delhi, April 2017.
By October 2026: 687 routes and 95 aerodromes (including 17 heliports, two water aerodromes).
Over 3.68 lakh flights carried 1.72 crore passengers.
Operational airports rose from 74 (2014) to 166 (2026); India is world's third-largest domestic aviation market.
Modified UDAN (4 July 2026): ₹28,840 crore, FY 2026–27 to 2035–36; 100 airports, 200 helipads.
u0251.hook: UDAN = 'Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik' – let the common citizen of the country fly.
u0251.trap: Don't confuse the launch (21 October 2016) with the first flight (Shimla–Delhi, April 2017).

mcq.q: UDAN completed 10 years in October 2026. Between which cities did the first UDAN flight operate in April 2017?
mcq.why: The first UDAN flight connected Shimla and Delhi in April 2017.

u0252.gist: The Supreme Court held that internet access is a fundamental right, including for children, and rejected blanket bans on children's internet use.
facts: Case: Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish; order delivered on October 15, 2026.
Bench: Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran.
Right flows from Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a); children have it irrespective of age.
Blanket limits called disproportionate; Court suggested parental supervision, child modes, private-by-default accounts.
Limits on inherently harmful content and services remain allowed.
Centre must build a National Hash & URL List Database to detect and remove CSEAM.

mcq.q: In October 2026, the Supreme Court recognised internet access as a fundamental right under Article 21 read with which provision?
mcq.why: The Court recognised it under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a).

u0253.gist: The Right to Information Act, 2005 completed 21 years of full implementation on 12 October 2026; it supports transparency and accountability in government.
facts: Presidential assent: 15 June 2005; fully operational: 12 October 2005.
Right to Know comes from Article 19(1)(a) – freedom of speech and expression.
State of U.P. v. Raj Narain (1975): SC recognised citizens' right to know about public acts.
PUCL v. Union of India (2003): voters' right to information about candidates upheld.
The RTI Act replaced the Freedom of Information Act, 2002.
It set up the Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions.
u0253.trap: Don't confuse assent (15 June 2005) with full operation (12 October 2005), the date used for the anniversary.

mcq.q: The RTI Act, 2005, which completed 21 years in October 2026, replaced which earlier law?
mcq.why: The RTI Act replaced the Freedom of Information Act, 2002.

u0254.gist: The National SARAS Mela 2026 in Vijayawada, under DAY-NRLM, showcased rural women entrepreneurs' products; it is the first National SARAS Mela outside Delhi-NCR.
facts: Held 13–31 October 2026 at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada.
Organised under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM).
About 1,500 SHG women and Lakhpati Didis from 34 states/UTs; more than 650 stalls.
Main attraction: a 16-foot installation, 'SHAKTI – The Spirit of Lakhpati Didi'.
First National SARAS Mela: Delhi, 1999, with about 65 beneficiaries.
So far 117 National SARAS Melas; annual sales exceed ₹200 crore.
u0254.trap: The first-ever SARAS Mela was in Delhi (1999); Vijayawada 2026 is the first National SARAS Mela outside Delhi-NCR.

mcq.q: The National SARAS Mela 2026, the first held outside Delhi-NCR, was organised in which city?
mcq.why: It was held 13–31 October 2026 at Punnami Ghat, Vijayawada, the first outside Delhi-NCR.

u0255.gist: On 11 October 2026 in Tamil Nadu, PM Modi opened the Poonamallee–Vadapalani stretch of Chennai Metro Phase II and launched highway, rail and port projects.
facts: Poonamallee–Vadapalani metro stretch cost about ₹4,900 crore.
It has a 3.7-km double-decker structure and signalling designed for driverless operation.
Highway projects (about ₹3,700 crore): 36-km Vadugapatti–Therkuvenganallur (NH-744), 30-km Madurai Ring Road (NH-744A).
Rail projects over ₹750 crore, including Karaikal–Peralam line; five Amrit Bharat Stations inaugurated.
Ports: four projects at Chennai Port, eight at V.O. Chidambaranar Port, Coal Berth-3 at Kamarajar Port.
Dedicated the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras.

mcq.q: The Poonamallee–Vadapalani stretch of Chennai Metro Phase II, opened in October 2026, has a double-decker structure of what length?
mcq.why: A distinctive feature of this corridor is its 3.7-kilometre-long double-decker structure.

u0256.gist: The Rural Development Ministry is starting DDU-GKY 2.0 training batches from October 2026, giving placement-linked skill training to poor rural youth.
facts: DDU-GKY: Centrally Sponsored Scheme, launched 25 September 2014 under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission.
For youth aged 15–35 from poor rural households; courses last three to twelve months.
DDU-GKY 2.0: targets of over nine lakh candidates given to all 31 participating states/UTs for 2026–28.
24 states/UTs allotted 5.6 lakh candidates across 1,200+ projects; about 2,015 batches for 70,000 youth.
Since 2014–15: 18.47 lakh trained for 800+ job types; 12.43 lakh got jobs.
Revised 2.0 guidelines: May 2025. Goa leads preparations; J&K allocated 100% targets, started 91%.
u0256.trap: DDU-GKY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2014 under NRLM; 2.0 is its new round for 2026–28.

mcq.q: DDU-GKY, whose 2.0 training batches began in October 2026, gives skill training to rural youth of which age group?
mcq.why: The scheme trains youth aged 15–35 years from poor rural households.

u0257.gist: On 6 October 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) as an SPV to plan and integrate all transport modes.
facts: ITLA is a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV); approved by the Cabinet chaired by PM Narendra Modi.
It will be the national apex body for integrated transport and logistics planning, research and appraisal.
It will prepare a National Transport Master Plan with a horizon of ten years or more.
It will technically appraise Government of India infrastructure projects costing ₹500 crore or more.
It will build a National Transport Data Repository (NTDR).
NTDR data: GSTN e-way bills, FASTag, Vahan, GPS systems and urban traffic systems.
u0257.hook: ITLA links four modes in one plan: road, rail, water and air.

mcq.q: The Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA), approved in October 2026, will appraise central infrastructure projects costing at least how much?
mcq.why: ITLA will appraise Government of India infrastructure projects costing ₹500 crore or more.

u0258.gist: UPSC completed 100 years on 1 October 2026; India's first Public Service Commission was set up on 1 October 1926.
facts: Centenary event 'Manthan': Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, 30 September–1 October 2026.
Lee Commission (1924, Arthur Hamilton Lee) recommended it; set up under PSC (Functions) Rules, 1926.
First Chairman: Sir Ross Barker; office at Metcalfe House, Delhi.
Renamed Federal PSC (1 April 1937), then Union PSC (26 January 1950).
1947: H.K. Kripalani first Indian Chairman; 1979: three-stage exam; 2011: CSAT introduced.
Satyendranath Tagore first Indian in ICS (joined 1864); ICS exam first held in India 1922 at Allahabad.
u0258.trap: Sir Ross Barker = first Chairman (1926); H.K. Kripalani = first Indian Chairman (1947). Tagore passed in 1863 but joined in 1864.

mcq.q: UPSC completed 100 years in 2026. Who was the first Chairman of India's Public Service Commission set up in 1926?
mcq.why: Sir Ross Barker, a member of the UK Home Civil Service, was its first Chairman.

mcq.q: UPSC completed 100 years in 2026. On which date was the Federal Public Service Commission renamed the Union Public Service Commission?
mcq.why: On 26 January 1950, the Federal PSC was renamed the Union Public Service Commission.

u0259.gist: The People's Plan Campaign 2026–27 began on 2 October 2026 to prepare Panchayat Development Plans for 2027–28 through citizen participation.
facts: Theme: 'Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas'; started on Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October 2026.
PPC, also called Jan Yojana Abhiyan, was first launched on 2 October 2018; held every year.
Over 2.42 lakh Special Gram Sabhas scheduled on GPDP and Panchayat NIRNAY portals.
Three levels: Gram (GPDP), Block (BPDP) and District (DPDP) Panchayat Development Plans.
SHG federations prepare Village Prosperity and Resilience Plans (VPRPs).
Over 2.55 lakh Gram Panchayats upload GPDPs on eGramSwaraj; 18.13 lakh plans uploaded (2019–20 to 2025–26).
u0259.trap: Campaign year 2026–27 prepares plans for financial year 2027–28.

mcq.q: What was the theme of the People's Plan Campaign 2026–27 launched on 2 October 2026?
mcq.why: PPC 2026–27 began on Gandhi Jayanti under the theme 'Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas'.

u0260.gist: Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav launched implementation guidelines of National Coastal Mission 2.0, linking coastal conservation, climate resilience and livelihoods.
facts: Guidelines launched on September 30, 2026 in New Delhi.
Central Sector Scheme of MoEFCC; outlay ₹767 crore for 2025–26 to 2030–31.
Earlier National Coastal Mission subsumed into NCM 2.0 from 16 May 2025.
NCM 1.0 (2021–22 to 2025–26) backed mangrove and coral-reef conservation and beach development.
Covers nine coastal States and four Union Territories.
Andaman & Nicobar: mangrove restoration; Gujarat: Conservation and Information Centre cum Marine Oceanarium planned.
u0260.trap: NCM 2.0 took over the old mission on 16 May 2025; only its guidelines came on 30 September 2026.

mcq.q: National Coastal Mission 2.0, whose guidelines were launched in September 2026, has what approved outlay for 2025–26 to 2030–31?
mcq.why: NCM 2.0 is a Central Sector Scheme with an approved outlay of ₹767 crore.

u0261.gist: Lakshadweep (11 October 2026) and Jammu & Kashmir (September 2026) were declared fully literate under the ULLAS adult literacy programme.
facts: Lakshadweep (11 Oct 2026, by Administrator Praful Patel) became fully literate; J&K was 10th since June 2024.
ULLAS = Understanding Lifelong Learning for All in Society; for people aged 15+ who missed school.
Fully literate = at least 95% of people aged 15 and above can read and write.
Firsts: Ladakh (24 June 2024) first administrative unit; Mizoram (20 May 2025) first state.
Sikkim fifth state (27 May 2026); Uttarakhand sixth state (8 July 2026, 98.7%).
Sikkim: first paperless State judiciary, declared 1 May 2026 by CJI Surya Kant in Gangtok.
u0261.hook: Ladakh first unit (2024), Mizoram first state (2025): L comes before M.
u0261.trap: Himachal was the fifth State/UT (fourth state, September 2025); Sikkim was the fifth state (May 2026).

mcq.q: Under the ULLAS programme, which state was declared India's first fully literate state in May 2025?
mcq.why: On 20 May 2025, Mizoram became the first state to attain full literacy under ULLAS.

mcq.q: Under ULLAS, a State/UT is declared fully literate when at least what share of people aged 15 and above can read and write?
mcq.why: A state or UT is fully literate once at least 95% of those aged 15+ are literate.

u0262.gist: Five heritage sites – four in Madhya Pradesh and the India–South Africa 'Sites of Satyagraha' – joined India's UNESCO Tentative List, taking it to 78.
facts: Announced on September 29, 2026; India's Tentative List now totals 78.
Bagh Cave Paintings: nine Buddhist caves beside the Baghni River (Madhya Pradesh).
Udayagiri Caves: 20 caves, mainly from late fourth and early fifth centuries, under Gupta patronage.
Chambal Valley Temples (Morena): Bateshwar, Padavali, Kakanmath; Nagara style; Gurjara-Pratihara and Kachchhapaghata patronage.
Ginnorgarh Fort: Raj Gond fortified capital in Sehore district.
Sites of Satyagraha: nine sites, seven in India and two in South Africa (incl. Phoenix Settlement).
u0262.hook: Pairs: Bagh – Baghni River; Ginnorgarh – Sehore; Chambal temples – Morena; Udayagiri – Gupta.

mcq.q: After five additions announced on September 29, 2026, how many entries are on India's UNESCO Tentative List?
mcq.why: The five new entries brought India's UNESCO Tentative List total to 78.

mcq.q: Ginnorgarh Fort, added to India's UNESCO Tentative List in September 2026, lies in which district of Madhya Pradesh?
mcq.why: Ginnorgarh Fort, a Raj Gond fortified capital, lies in Sehore district.

u0263.gist: The 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah was launched on 9 September 2026 in Varanasi, putting Anganwadi Centres at the centre of the fight against malnutrition.
facts: Venue: Rudraksh International Cooperation and Convention Centre, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh.
Led by the Ministry of Women and Child Development; ran 9 September–8 October 2026.
Theme: 'Hamari Anganwadi, Hamari Jimmedari' (Our Anganwadi, Our Responsibility).
Poshan Maah = National Nutrition Month, observed every September under the POSHAN framework.
Five priorities include dietary diversity and protein, hot-cooked meals, and maternal nutrition with PMMVY.
u0263.hook: The 9th edition began on the 9th (9 September).

mcq.q: What was the theme of the 9th Rashtriya Poshan Maah launched in Varanasi in September 2026?
mcq.why: Its official theme was 'Hamari Anganwadi, Hamari Jimmedari' (Our Anganwadi, Our Responsibility).

u0264.gist: Five cheetah cubs born at Kuno on 5 October 2026 took India's cheetah count to 60; after one cub died, it fell to 59.
facts: Mother KJP21 (32 months, Indian-born) is the third Indian-born female to give birth; father from Botswana.
Indian-born cheetahs: 41 after the births, 40 after the Aasha cub died (12 October 2026).
Project Cheetah launched at Kuno on 17 September 2022 with eight Namibian cheetahs.
Imports: eight from Namibia, 12 from South Africa (2023), nine from Botswana (2026); total 29.
Programme expanded to Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary (Madhya Pradesh) in 2025.
Project uses African cheetah (A. j. jubatus); India's native Asiatic subspecies (A. j. venaticus) is Critically Endangered.
u0264.trap: Total population 60 → 59, but Indian-born 41 → 40; cumulative imports are 29.
u0264.check: Botswana is said to have handed over eight cheetahs in November 2025, but nine arrived from Botswana on 28 February 2026.

mcq.q: Project Cheetah was launched at Kuno National Park on 17 September 2022 with cheetahs from which country?
mcq.why: PM Modi released eight Namibian cheetahs into quarantine enclosures at Kuno.

mcq.q: After a cheetah cub died on 12 October 2026, what was India's total cheetah population?
mcq.why: Births took the count to 60; after the Aasha cub's death it became 59.

u0265.gist: Bhupender Yadav gave the first PRAMAAN certificates under the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme, moving it from policy to ground-level use.
facts: Presented in New Delhi on September 29, 2026.
Scheme: Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS), launched by the Ministry in December 2023.
Operating agency: Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM), Bhopal.
First certificates: Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation (33,000 hectares of plantations) and farmer Govind Mohapatra (Odisha).
PRAMAAN = Programme for Recognition and Accreditation of Sustainable Management Practices for Agroforestry And Natural Forestry Resources.
PRAMAAN is an important tool for Indian producers, exporters and forest-based enterprises.
u0265.hook: PRAMAAN sounds like 'प्रमाण' (proof): a certificate that proves sustainable forestry.

mcq.q: Which institute is the operating agency of the scheme under which the first PRAMAAN certificates were given in September 2026?
o: Indian Institute of Forest Management, Bhopal
Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education
mcq.why: The event was organised by the IFWCS operating agency, IIFM Bhopal.

u0266.gist: Hardeep Puri launched the unified GOBARdhan scheme on 1 October 2026 to grow India's Compressed Biogas sector using farm, cattle and city waste.
facts: GOBARdhan = Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan; Cabinet approved it on 6 August 2026.
Central Sector Scheme led by Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; ₹23,731 crore for FY 2026-27 to 2035-36.
Converts crop residue, cattle dung and municipal organic waste into clean energy and organic manure.
Original GOBARdhan began in 2018 under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen).
Unified scheme merges CBG parts earlier run by four ministries; builds on SATAT.
By 6 August 2026: 1,908 registered plants, 217 commissioned, 339 under construction.
u0266.hook: GOBAR-dhan: cow dung (गोबर) turned into wealth (धन).
u0266.trap: Cabinet approval 6 August 2026 vs formal launch 1 October 2026; the original GOBARdhan dates to 2018.

mcq.q: The unified GOBARdhan scheme for Compressed Biogas, launched in October 2026, is led by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
mcq.why: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas leads it, with a ₹23,731 crore outlay.

u0267.gist: Bharat Taxi, India's first cooperative-led ride-hailing platform, launched in five Uttar Pradesh cities on 23 September 2026 on a 'Driver is the Owner' model.
facts: UP cities: Lucknow, Gorakhpur, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj.
Operator: Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), registered under Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002.
STCL established 6 June 2025; national launch 5 February 2026.
Authorised share capital ₹300 crore, in shares of ₹100 each.
Drivers are called Saarthis (also Sarathis); services include cab, auto, bike and rentals.
Safety: driver and vehicle checks, trip records, SOS and journey-sharing.
u0267.trap: Three dates: STCL set up 6 June 2025, national launch 5 February 2026, UP launch 23 September 2026.

mcq.q: Bharat Taxi, launched in five Uttar Pradesh cities in September 2026, is operated by which body?
o: Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation
mcq.why: The operator is Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited, a multi-state cooperative society.

u0268.gist: India Justice Report's first Consumer Justice Report 2026 ranked states on consumer commission capacity; Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya topped their categories.
facts: Released March 2026; title 'Assessing the Capacity of Redressal Commissions in India'.
Five themes, 11 equally weighted indicators; score out of ten; 19 large/mid and nine small states ranked.
Top: Andhra Pradesh (6.28) large/mid; Meghalaya (5.58) small; Uttar Pradesh 10th (4.36).
Pending cases rose about 21%: 4.27 lakh (end 2019) to 5.15 lakh (end 2024).
About 35% of cases pending over three years; Kerala about 79%, Uttar Pradesh about 62%.
CVC's 62nd Annual Report (2025): CVOs got 70,584 complaints directly; 64,905 disposed.
u0268.trap: IJR's report ranks consumer commissions; the CVC report (also in this news) is about vigilance complaints.

mcq.q: Which state ranked first among large and mid-sized states in the India Justice Report's Consumer Justice Report 2026?
mcq.why: Andhra Pradesh ranked first with a score of 6.28 out of 10.

mcq.q: In the Consumer Justice Report 2026, what was Uttar Pradesh's rank among large and mid-sized states?
mcq.why: Uttar Pradesh ranked 10 with a score of 4.36.

u0269.gist: The Jal Shakti Ministry released First Census of Springs reports on 25 September 2026; Volume II Part II counted 14,468 springs in ten states.
facts: Released at the valedictory of the ninth India International Water Week, Bharat Mandapam; chaired by C. R. Patil.
Manipur has the most springs (3,941), followed by Maharashtra (3,652).
Reference year 2023–24; figures cover only these ten states, not all of India.
States: Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Goa, Maharashtra, Manipur, Odisha, Rajasthan, Telangana, Tripura, West Bengal.
Rajasthan recorded the fewest (13); Andhra Pradesh's 34 springs are all seasonal.
Earlier Volume II (Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Ladakh, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu) came out on 23 March 2026.
u0269.trap: 14,468 is a ten-state total, not an all-India spring count.

mcq.q: According to Volume II, Part II of India's First Census of Springs (September 2026), which state has the most springs?
mcq.why: Of 14,468 springs in ten states, Manipur recorded the largest number, followed by Maharashtra.

u0270.gist: A 17 September 2026 update on the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme reported 106 approved projects across 15 States, with expected investment of ₹69,548 crore.
facts: Electronics exports rose from over ₹38,000 crore (FY 2014–15) to ₹4.24 lakh crore (FY 2025–26).
As of August 2026: manufacturing started at 38 plants; 16 projects at advanced stages.
ECMS notified on 8 April 2025; outlay raised from ₹22,919 crore to ₹40,000 crore in Budget 2026–27.
Turnover-linked incentives for six years (plus optional one-year gestation); capex incentives for five years.
Electronics production rose from ₹1.9 lakh crore (FY 2014–15) to ₹13.11 lakh crore (FY 2025–26).
National target by 2030: $500 billion electronics manufacturing and $150 billion exports.
u0270.trap: India's 2030 targets ($500 billion ecosystem, $150 billion exports) are separate from ECMS project outcomes.

mcq.q: The outlay of the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) was raised to how much in the Union Budget 2026–27?
mcq.why: The initial outlay of ₹22,919 crore was increased to ₹40,000 crore in Budget 2026–27.

u0271.gist: The Home Ministry reportedly proposed Article 371-K to give Ladakh special constitutional safeguards with a directly elected UT-level body; it remains a proposal.
facts: Proposed at a 9 September 2026 meeting with Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA).
Body would make laws on land, culture, language, forests, environment and natural resources.
'Sui generis' model = unique arrangement; no automatic statehood or regular UT legislature.
Ladakh became a UT without a legislature on October 31, 2019 (J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019).
Local demands: statehood, Sixth Schedule, job safeguards, separate Lok Sabha seats for Leh and Kargil.
Sixth Schedule (Articles 244(2), 275(1)) covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram.
u0271.hook: Sixth Schedule states = 'AMTM': Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram.
u0271.trap: Article 371-K is only a proposal; it is not statehood and not Sixth Schedule status.

mcq.q: In September 2026, the Union Home Ministry reportedly proposed which Article to give special constitutional safeguards to Ladakh?
mcq.why: MHA reportedly proposed Article 371-K for Ladakh at a 9 September 2026 meeting.

u0272.gist: Ladakh LG Vinai Kumar Saxena opened twin flower fields in Leh on 17 September 2026, described as the world's highest-altitude twin flower fields.
facts: Opened on Sewa Diwas to mark PM Narendra Modi's 76th birthday.
Located at Choglamsar and Stakna; altitude 10,600 feet; 40 acres together.
Over 25 lakh flowers: about 24 lakh Lilium and 1 lakh Gladiolus.
Foundation stone laid on June 22, 2026; MoU with CSIR–IHBT, Palampur (Himachal Pradesh).
Agriculture Department develops the fields, then hands them to SHGs and cooperatives at bloom.
First air consignment (29 September 2026): 15,000 A-grade Lilium stems from KBR Airport, Leh, for Delhi, Mumbai, Chandigarh.

mcq.q: The twin flower fields opened in Leh on 17 September 2026 are at Choglamsar and which other place?
mcq.why: The fields are located at Choglamsar and Stakna, at 10,600 feet.

u0273.gist: Indian Railways approved Kavach 4.0, the train-protection system, for remaining sections of North Eastern Railway's Varanasi and Izzatnagar divisions.
facts: Varanasi division: announced September 28, 2026; ₹223 crore; 614.75 route km.
Izzatnagar division: announced August 12, 2026; ₹295 crore (estimated); 660 route km.
Kavach was developed by RDSO (Research Designs and Standards Organisation) with Indian industry.
Functions: enforce permitted speed, prevent Signal Passing at Danger (SPAD), reduce collision risk.
RDSO approved the Kavach 4.0 specification on 16 July 2024.
4.0 upgrades: better location accuracy, signal data in big yards, OFC station link, electronic interlocking interface.
u0273.trap: Varanasi: ₹223 crore, 614.75 km; Izzatnagar: ₹295 crore, 660 km – don't swap.

mcq.q: Which organisation developed Kavach, approved in Version 4.0 for NER's Varanasi division in September 2026?
mcq.why: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) developed Kavach with Indian industry.

u0274.gist: Assam's Uniform Civil Code Act, 2026 got Presidential assent on 29 September 2026, making Assam the first Northeast state with a UCC.
facts: Bill introduced 25 May 2026 by Atul Bora; passed by voice vote on 27 May 2026.
Assam is the third state, after Uttarakhand and Gujarat, to adopt a state UCC law.
Linked to Article 44; STs excluded; repeals Assam Compulsory Registration of Muslim Marriages and Divorces Act, 2024.
Monogamy compulsory; bigamy/polygamy up to seven years' jail; marriage age 21 (men), 18 (women).
Marriage memorandum within 60 days; live-in registration within one month; live-in children fully legitimate.
Gujarat UCC: assent 17 September 2026; committee led by Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai.
u0274.hook: UCC order: Uttarakhand → Gujarat → Assam (first in the Northeast).
u0274.trap: Assam: passed 27 May, assent 29 September 2026. Gujarat: passed 24 March, assent 17 September 2026.

mcq.q: With Presidential assent in September 2026, Assam became the third state to adopt a UCC law. Which two states came before it?
mcq.why: Assam became the third state after Uttarakhand and Gujarat to adopt UCC legislation.

mcq.q: Under the Assam Uniform Civil Code Act, 2026, within what time must a live-in relationship be registered?
mcq.why: The Act makes registration of live-in relationships mandatory within one month.

u0275.gist: UP's Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana makes long-term farm loans cheaper for small and marginal farmers, at 6% interest with state support.
facts: Announced by CM Yogi Adityanath on 21 December 2025 at Yuva Sahkar Sammelan and UP Cooperative Expo 2025.
UP Cabinet approved it on September 15, 2026; CM launched it in Lucknow on 23 September 2026.
Loans up to ₹6 lakh for eligible small and marginal farmers.
Farmer pays 6% a year (earlier 11%); State gives 5% interest support for on-time repayment.
Mini Nandini scheme: 10 indigenous cows (Sahiwal, Gir, Tharparkar); 50% subsidy up to ₹11.80 lakh.
Mukhyamantri Krishak Durghatna Kalyan Yojana: ₹5 lakh on accidental death of an eligible farmer.
u0275.hook: 11% − 5% state support = 6% paid by the farmer.
u0275.trap: The 5% interest support is only for farmers who pay instalments on time.
u0275.check: Nandini scheme supports 25-cow units, yet a 'unit with five Gangatiri cows' has a ₹30.50 lakh ceiling; this looks inconsistent.
hindi: Small and marginal farmers (लघु एवं सीमांत किसान)

mcq.q: Under UP's Mukhyamantri Krishak Samriddhi Yojana (launched September 2026), what interest rate do eligible farmers pay?
mcq.why: Beneficiary rate is 6% per annum, down from 11%, with 5% state interest support.

u0276.gist: PM Modi inaugurated SEMICON India 2026, the fifth edition, at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, as India moves to the Semicon 2.0 programme.
facts: Held 17–19 September 2026; theme 'Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem'.
Over 600 exhibitors, 52 countries, six country and 12 state pavilions; 51,656 registrations, about 40,000 footfall; 56 MoUs.
Semicon 1.0: 12 units approved, over ₹1.64 lakh crore investment; nine are packaging units.
CDIL Semiconductor (Mohali) and Suchi Semicon (Surat) lines launched; five of 12 now operational.
Semicon 2.0: approved 15 July 2026, outlay ₹1,27,500 crore; six pillars notified 31 August 2026.
Targets: support 200 design start-ups; train one lakh technicians in five years.
u0276.trap: SEMICON India 2026 = fifth edition of the event; Semicon 2.0 = the government programme (₹1,27,500 crore).

mcq.q: SEMICON India 2026, the fifth edition, was held at which venue?
mcq.why: PM inaugurated it on 17 September 2026 at Yashobhoomi, the India International Convention and Expo Centre.

mcq.q: What is the budget outlay of Semicon 2.0, approved by the Union Cabinet on 15 July 2026?
mcq.why: The Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0 on 15 July 2026 with a ₹1,27,500 crore outlay.

u0277.gist: The Status of Policing in India Report 2026 by Common Cause and Lokniti-CSDS studied cybercrime victims, linking bribery and contacts with recovering lost money.
facts: Released in New Delhi on 24 September 2026; theme 'Cybercrime – Victim Perspectives and Systemic Responses'.
Survey: 8,306 citizens in 15 States and Delhi.
NCRB: cybercrime cases rose 17.9%, from 86,420 (2023) to 1,01,928 (2024).
13% of respondents faced cybercrime in the past two to three years; 54% of victims faced financial fraud.
Those who paid a bribe: 38% full recovery; those who did not: 12%.
Common scam calls: unordered deliveries (33%), high-return investments (31%), fake bank officials (27%).

mcq.q: The Status of Policing in India Report 2026, focused on cybercrime, was released by Common Cause and which organisation?
o: Bureau of Police Research and Development
mcq.why: SPIR 2026 was released by Common Cause and Lokniti-CSDS on 24 September 2026.

u0278.gist: The NCDC (Amendment) Act, 2026 widens the National Co-operative Development Corporation's mandate and lending powers, without extra central budget support.
facts: Amends NCDC Act, 1962; NCDC is a statutory body (set up 1963) under the Ministry of Cooperation.
Introduced in Lok Sabha 10 August; passed Lok Sabha 11 August, Rajya Sabha 12 August 2026.
President's assent: 14 August 2026; commencement needs a separate notification (Section 1(2)).
Allows direct loans and grants to any cooperative society or eligible entity.
'Foodstuffs' widened to processed food; rural-area limit on cooperative industrial activity removed.
97th Constitutional Amendment (2011): Article 19(1)(c), Article 43B and Part IXB on cooperatives.
u0278.trap: The NCDC Act is of 1962, but NCDC itself was established in 1963.

mcq.q: The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011, recalled with the NCDC (Amendment) Act 2026, introduced which Article on cooperatives?
mcq.why: The 97th Amendment introduced Article 43B, promoting voluntary formation and autonomy of cooperatives.

u0279.gist: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026 raised puisne judges from 33 to 37, taking total strength to 38 judges.
facts: Total sanctioned strength: 34 to 38 judges, including the CJI; first increase since 2019.
Cabinet approved four more judges on 5 May 2026; Lok Sabha passed it by voice vote (3 August).
Presidential assent: 11 August 2026.
Original 1956 Act allowed 10 judges plus the CJI (total 11).
Reason: pendency – 92,101 cases on 1 January 2026; 92,823 by 30 April 2026 (NJDG).
In 2025 the Court received 75,410 cases but disposed of 65,615 (gap 9,795).
u0279.hook: 33 + four = 37 puisne judges; add the CJI = 38.
u0279.trap: Puisne judges exclude the CJI (37); total strength includes the CJI (38).
hindi: Chief Justice of India (भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश)

mcq.q: After the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026, what is the Court's total sanctioned strength including the CJI?
mcq.why: Puisne judges rose from 33 to 37, so total strength rose from 34 to 38.

u0280.gist: The Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026 creates a judiciary-led National Tribunals Commission to keep tribunals independent of the executive, replacing the 2021 Act.
facts: Introduced by Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal; Lok Sabha passed it by voice vote on August 10, 2026.
Assent: August 13, 2026; in force from August 25, 2026.
Repeals the 2021 Act; applies to 16 tribunals, appellate tribunals and authorities.
Implements Madras Bar Association v. Union of India principles; SC had struck down 2021 Act provisions.
National Tribunals Commission: headquarters New Delhi; one Chairperson and four members (total five).
NTC members serve five years or till age 70, whichever is earlier.
u0280.trap: Assent on 13 August 2026, but in force from 25 August 2026.

mcq.q: Under the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026, how many members, including the Chairperson, will the National Tribunals Commission have?
mcq.why: One Chairperson and four members give a total strength of five.

u0281.gist: On Swachh Vayu Diwas, 7 September 2026, the 5th Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards ranked NCAP cities; Lucknow topped cities above 10 lakh population.
facts: Held on International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies; Chief Guest: NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava.
Above 10 lakh: Lucknow (198), Indore (197), Jabalpur (195); Madurai lowest (132.1).
3–10 lakh: Rourkela first (198.5); below 3 lakh: Kalinga first (198.5), Byrnihat last (108.5).
Best ward (above 30,000 population): Zone4Ward70, Lucknow; Pryj31, Allahabad, third in its category.
NCAP launched January 10, 2019; covers 130 cities in 24 States/UTs; ₹16,425 crore performance grant.
FY 2025-26: 108 of 130 cities improved PM10 over 2017-18; 14 cities met national standards.
u0281.hook: Lucknow wins twice: top city (198) and top ward (Zone4Ward70).
u0281.trap: Rourkela (3–10 lakh) and Kalinga (below 3 lakh) both scored 198.5 – same score, different categories.

mcq.q: Which city ranked first among cities with population above 10 lakh in the 5th Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026?
mcq.why: In Category I, Lucknow topped with score 198, ahead of Indore (197).

mcq.q: When was the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), whose cities were ranked in Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan 2026, launched?
mcq.why: NCAP was launched on January 10, 2019 and covers 130 cities.

u0282.gist: The Panchayati Raj Ministry launched DAANVEER, a voluntary platform for citizens to donate verified digital-equipment bundles directly to Gram Panchayats.
facts: Launched on July 29, 2026 by MoPR Secretary Vivek Bharadwaj at Krishi Bhawan, New Delhi.
Tagline: 'Give Back to Your Village'.
Works through the Meri Panchayat app linked with the DigiHaat marketplace.
Donors choose pre-approved computer bundles matched to State-specific technical specifications.
Developed by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj with NIC and DigiHaat.
Related platforms: SabhaSaar (AI minutes of Gram Sabhas), Gram Manchitra (GIS planning), eGramSwaraj (accounts).
u0282.hook: DAANVEER = daan (donation) + veer (brave): donors are the village's heroes.

mcq.q: DAANVEER, launched by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj in July 2026, works through which citizen app?
mcq.why: Citizens give digital-equipment bundles to Gram Panchayats through the Meri Panchayat application.

u0283.gist: PM Modi launched the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan on 2 August 2026 to mobilise youth for a drug-free India.
facts: Launched by video conference with over one crore youth at over 28,000 locations.
Backed by more than 125 spiritual and public organisations, institutions and NGOs.
Began as a 2025 pilot in Kashi (Uttar Pradesh) under the Kashi Declaration.
Runs for 100 weeks – 100 consecutive Sundays of art, sports, meditation and service activities.
PM called the youth the 'Amrit generation' and recovered addicts 'true warriors'.
u0283.hook: 100 Sundays = 100 steps towards a drug-free India.

mcq.q: The 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', launched in August 2026, began as a pilot project in which city?
mcq.why: It originated as a pilot project in Kashi, Uttar Pradesh, in 2025.

u0284.gist: The MMDR Amendment Act, 2026 brings mineral-bearing land under central control and limits State taxes on mineral rights.
facts: Passed by both Houses on August 13, 2026; assent August 17, 2026; in force August 22, 2026.
Amends the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957; it is Act No. 20 of 2026.
Background: July 2024, nine-judge bench (8:1) held royalty is a contractual payment, not a tax.
That case: Mineral Area Development Authority v. Steel Authority of India; States may tax under Entry 50.
Section 9D restricts State taxes, cesses and levies on mineral rights and mineral-bearing land.
Unpaid past State levies become invalid; amounts already paid will not be refunded.
u0284.trap: Royalty is a contractual payment, not a tax (8:1 ruling, July 2024).

mcq.q: In the Mineral Area Development Authority case (July 2024), cited with the MMDR Amendment Act 2026, the Supreme Court held royalty to be what?
mcq.why: A nine-judge bench ruled 8:1 that royalty is a contractual payment, not a tax.
